notes.text: CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.

notes.text: Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.

cwe.name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere

notes.text:
The Genesys demo page — deployed publicly at `https://ssagov.github.io/genesys/demo/genesys-demo.html` and linked from the repository README — loads executable JavaScript from `cdn.polyfill.io`, a domain that was **sold to Funnull Technology Inc. in February 2024** and **served malicious payloads** (device-fingerprinted redirects to sports-betting and scam sites via `googie-anaiytics.com`) **in June 2024**. Google suspended Ads for embedding sites, Namecheap suspended the domain, Cloudflare and Fastly stood up safe mirrors, and the hostname is on Google Safe Browsing and uBlock Origin blocklists. Ownership of the domain remains with the hostile party.

The vendored Mavo v0.2.0 bundle — the library behind the toolkit's data-persistence feature (the release notes record "Added Data Persistence (Mavo)" at `docs/Release-Notes.md:179`, and the demo template loads the bundle at `demo/genesys-demo.html:36`) — contains a second, runtime reference: when browser feature-detection finds any missing capability, Mavo dynamically injects a `<script>` for `https://cdn.polyfill.io/v2/polyfill.min.js?unknown=polyfill&features=…`. This propagates the compromised reference into downstream prototypes built from the toolkit, which the README describes as ranging up to production-ready user interfaces.

The `ssagov.github.io` origin carries no session, authentication, or user data, which bounds CVSS impact at `L/L/L`. The finding is rated High rather than the Medium normally assigned to no-SRI CDN loads because the third party is not a trusted CDN operator who might be compromised — **it is a hostile-owned domain that has already served malware from this exact URL**. SRI would not mitigate (the domain owner controls the response); removal is the only fix.
